name: State of the Union Address
description: The constitutionally mandated annual message to Congress, delivered before a joint session in the House chamber of the United States Capitol and carried live by every broadcast and cable news network from a shared camera pool. Nielsen counted 15 networks on the 2026 address.

name: Presidential Address to a Joint Session of Congress
description: A newly inaugurated president's first address to a joint session of Congress, staged in the House chamber under the same pool camera and network simulcast arrangements as the State of the Union but not formally titled one. The most recent was delivered on 4 March 2025 and carried by 15 networks.

name: Presidential Inauguration
description: The quadrennial swearing-in ceremony at the United States Capitol, held on 20 January under the Twentieth Amendment and staged on the Capitol's West Front since 1981. The Joint Congressional Committee on Inaugural Ceremonies builds the platform and runs the ceremony; the Presidential Inaugural Committee produces the parade and evening balls. The 2025 ceremony was moved indoors to the Capitol Rotunda because of cold, the first such move since 1985.

name: Joint Session of Congress to Count Electoral Votes
description: The quadrennial joint session in the House chamber at which Congress opens and counts the electoral votes, carried live from the House floor pool feed. Federal law sets the session for 6 January following the meeting of the electors, moving to 7 January when the 6th is a Sunday.

name: Democratic National Convention
description: A four-night arena build with a purpose-built stage, network skyboxes and a separate media workspace, produced by the party's convention committee and carried across roughly fifteen networks each night. The 2028 convention has an announced date but no host city: the DNC narrowed the field to Boston, Denver and Philadelphia in August 2026.

name: Republican National Convention
description: A four-night arena build with a purpose-built stage, network skyboxes and an adjacent media centre, carried across roughly fifteen networks each night. Houston was named the 2028 host city in August 2023; the RNC has not set the dates, and the host organisation expects the build to centre on Toyota Center with the George R. Brown Convention Center and Minute Maid Park in support.

name: General Election Presidential Debates
description: Head-to-head general election debates, built as a single-set studio or hall production by the host network and simulcast to every other network from a shared feed. The 2024 cycle was arranged directly between the campaigns and the host networks rather than through the Commission on Presidential Debates: CNN produced the 27 June debate from its Atlanta studios with no audience, and ABC News produced the 10 September debate from the National Constitution Center in Philadelphia. No 2028 debate has been scheduled.

name: Vice Presidential Debate
description: The single vice presidential debate of a general election cycle, produced by one host network and simulcast to the rest. CBS News staged the 2024 debate at the CBS Broadcast Center in New York on 1 October, where Nielsen counted 43.15 million viewers across 15 networks. No 2028 debate has been scheduled.

name: Election Night Coverage
description: The networks' results broadcasts on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November — decision desks, touchscreen result walls, purpose-built studios and dozens of remote positions, all for one night. Nielsen counted 42.3 million viewers across 18 networks on 5 November 2024.

name: Iowa Caucuses
description: The first Republican nominating contest of a presidential cycle and the broadcast that goes with it: networks move anchor desks and satellite trucks to Des Moines for the week and originate most of a day's programming from Iowa. The 2028 Republican calendar had not been adopted as of August 2026, and Iowa Democrats are not among the party's approved early states.

name: New Hampshire Primary
description: The first-in-the-nation presidential primary and a week-long remote broadcast operation for the networks, which base anchor positions and result studios in the state. The date is set by the New Hampshire Secretary of State rather than by either national party, and the state has previously scheduled ahead of the party-sanctioned slot: the DNC's 2028 calendar places New Hampshire on 8 February 2028, but the state has not set its own date and no edition date is recorded here.

name: South Carolina Democratic Presidential Primary
description: The opening contest of the Democratic nominating calendar from 2028, and a full remote broadcast for the news networks, which set up result studios and anchor positions in the state for primary week. The DNC voted in August 2026 to place South Carolina first, on 22 January 2028.

name: Super Tuesday
description: The largest multi-state primary night of a presidential cycle and the biggest results broadcast between the early states and election night: a full decision-desk operation, a results studio and remote positions in a dozen or more states. Sixteen states and one territory voted on 5 March 2024; the 2028 date has not been set.

description: Network-hosted primary debates staged in arenas and theatres with a party-sanctioned candidate lectern set. Fox News opened the 2024 cycle from Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee on 23 August 2023, an exclusive broadcast simulcast on Rumble. No 2028-cycle debate schedule has been announced.

name: Democratic Presidential Primary Debates
description: Network-hosted primary debates staged as a two-night theatre build when the field is too large for one stage. NBC News, MSNBC and Telemundo opened the 2020 cycle from the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts in Miami on 26 and 27 June 2019, with a five-moderator desk and a simultaneous Spanish-language feed. No 2028-cycle debate schedule has been announced.

name: White House Correspondents' Association Dinner
description: The White House Correspondents' Association's annual black-tie dinner, normally held on the last Saturday in April in the International Ballroom of the Washington Hilton and carried live gavel-to-gavel by C-SPAN. The 2026 dinner was rescheduled from 25 April to 24 July and moved to a smaller ballroom at the Waldorf Astoria in Washington, with a reduced guest list, added security screening and no red-carpet arrivals line.

name: Alfred E. Smith Memorial Foundation Dinner
description: A white-tie charity dinner held on the third Thursday of October at the Waldorf Astoria New York, and in presidential years a televised set-piece at which both major-party nominees speak. The 80th dinner returned to the Waldorf Astoria on 16 October 2025 after eight years elsewhere while the hotel was closed for renovation.

description: A multi-day conference built around a main-stage broadcast set with a livestreamed speaker programme, a radio row and an exhibition hall. Long a fixture at the Gaylord National Resort in National Harbor, Maryland, it has moved between Gaylord properties in recent years: the Gaylord Texan in Grapevine in 2026 and the Gaylord Palms near Orlando in 2027.
